title: Chronicle Seal Kit: certified HSM manifests and retention automation for admin audit trails
creator: Noah Patel
description:
Problem statement: Customers in regulated industries require tamper-evident, region-bound admin audit trails (admin actions, privileged access, config changes) that are stored immutably, can be certified by a signed manifest, and can be exported as legally defensible evidence packages. Current audit capture pipeline reliably records events but lacks an end-to-end immutable sealing and certified export path that ties records to a KMS/HSM-backed attestation and retention policy enforcement.

Goal: Deliver the 'Chronicle Seal Kit' — a composable backend and operational workflow that: (1) produces an append-only sealed archive for admin events with WORM semantics; (2) attaches an HSM-signed custody manifest for each sealed epoch; (3) exposes retention policy controls (per-org, per-region) and an automated retention lifecycle (seal, hold, expire) with auditability; (4) provides an evidence-export API and console flow to produce certified packages for compliance/legal requests.

Scope: Implementation covers the audit-tail append pipeline, sealed-object storage layer (immutable object or S3-object-lock style), manifest generation and HSM signing, retention lifecycle engine, export APIs, console UX for retention & export, and observability (proof verification, export audit). Out of scope: schema changes to existing audit event payloads and long-term legal escrow beyond the export artifact (those are separate follow-ups).

Key design decisions: 
- Use segmented sealed epochs (time-windowed bundles) rather than per-event notarization to reduce HSM usage and cost (we will compute a Merkle root per epoch and sign it with HSM).
- Persist sealed blobs to region-bound immutable buckets (S3 Object Lock or equivalent). Each blob will include an index with event ranges and a manifest referencing cryptographic anchors.
- HSM signing workflow: sign(MerkleRoot || epoch_metadata) using customer or Redwood-managed KMS/HSM depending on tenancy (private vs hosted). Store signed manifests alongside sealed blobs and include an optional external anchoring record (timestamping service or ledger) for extra non-repudiation.
- Retention model: policy objects are declarative (retention_period, legal_hold_flag, region_affinity). The retention engine enforces transitions: sealed -> legal_hold -> eligible_for_expiry. Deletions are executed as manifested expiry artifacts for auditability.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) For a given admin-action stream, produce sealed epoch blobs and an HSM-signed manifest that verifies (crypto verification script returns OK).
2) Sealed blobs are stored with immutability semantics in the region specified by the tenant.
3) Retention policy changes via the console or API are enforced within the configured SLA (15 min) and generate audit events.
4) Evidence-export API returns a downloadable package with sealed blobs, signed manifests, and a machine-readable verification-checklist; package has a human-readable certificate (signed).
5) End-to-end tests cover manifest verification, export reproduction, legal hold, and scheduled expiry simulations.

Rollout plan: 
- Phase 1 (internal): implement sealing pipeline and local signing simulation; unit + e2e tests.
- Phase 2 (staged): wire up Redwood-managed HSM signing, store sealed blobs to staging immutable buckets, add retention engine. Enable feature-flag for internal customers.
- Phase 3 (pilot): support tenant-scoped HSM keys and region residency enforcement; run pilot with two customers under NDA.
- Phase 4 (GA): console controls, export UI, public docs and runbook.

Monitoring & metrics: sealed_epoch_count, seal_latency_ms (ingest -> sealed manifest), manifest_verification_failures, retention_enforcement_lag, export_job_success_rate, hsm_sign_rate and hsm_errors.

Security & compliance notes: This requires a security review (HSM key usage, signing canonicalization, export package integrity). All signing operations must be non-exportable keys. For private deployments we will support customer-managed HSMs; hosted uses Redwood KMS with restricted operator roles.
